payload.rationale:
The event asks if the maximum temperature in Austin on Sep 19, 2026, will be exactly 98°F or 99°F. The forecast information cutoff is the evening before the target date (Austin local time), but no current weather forecast is provided. Without a specific forecast, the estimate must rely on historical climatology. In late September, the average high temperature in Austin is typically around 89-91°F with a standard deviation of roughly 5 to 7 degrees. A high of 98-99°F represents an unusually hot day, about 1.3 to 1.6 standard deviations above normal. The probability of landing in this specific 2-degree bin based purely on climatology is relatively low, estimated at around 5-8%.

Strongest reason the estimate could be too high: The actual forecast for this specific day might be significantly cooler (e.g., a cold front dropping highs into the 70s or 80s, or rain), which would make the true probability near zero.

Strongest reason the estimate could be too low: Austin has been experiencing increasingly hot Septembers due to climate trends. If a late-season heatwave is currently occurring, the probability of hitting this exact temperature range could be much higher than the historical base rate.
limitations: No current weather forecast or observations for Austin on or leading up to September 19, 2026, are available.
Relies entirely on historical climatological base rates rather than real-time meteorological data.
